title: UART, I2C, and SPI: choosing a bus

questions.prompt: Which option states the main idea of “UART, I2C, and SPI: choosing a bus” correctly?
options: 1-Wire connects compatible devices on one bus with few wires.
I2S carries digital audio using bit clock (BCLK), word select (WS/LRCLK), and data lines.
UART is asynchronous point-to-point serial using TX/RX and common ground
CAN is a noise-tolerant differential, message-based bus used in vehicle ECUs, industrial control, and robotics.
questions.answer: UART is asynchronous point-to-point serial using TX/RX and common ground
questions.explanation: UART is asynchronous point-to-point serial using TX/RX and common ground

questions.prompt: Which additional fact about “UART, I2C, and SPI: choosing a bus” is accurate?
options: It connects digital microphones, DACs, and audio codecs
ESP32 calls its CAN 2.0 controller peripheral TWAI
DS18B20 measures temperature digitally and has a unique identifier.

questions.prompt: Which practical detail should be considered when using “UART, I2C, and SPI: choosing a bus”?
options: The data line needs a suitable pull-up
it is not UART or I2C.
controller pins cannot connect directly to CAN wiring.
I2C shares SDA/SCL and addresses among devices and needs pull-ups.
questions.answer: I2C shares SDA/SCL and addresses among devices and needs pull-ups.
questions.explanation: I2C shares SDA/SCL and addresses among devices and needs pull-ups.

questions.prompt: Which statement from the “UART, I2C, and SPI: choosing a bus” lesson is correct?
options: wiring and power matter on long cables.
Important note A separate CAN transceiver is required.
SPI uses SCK/MOSI/MISO plus a CS line per device for fast full-duplex transfer.
Sample rate, slot width, and mono/stereo format must match.
questions.answer: SPI uses SCK/MOSI/MISO plus a CS line per device for fast full-duplex transfer.
questions.explanation: SPI uses SCK/MOSI/MISO plus a CS line per device for fast full-duplex transfer.
